title: Enforcement of Approach Stabilization Gates
summary: Strict adherence to 1,000 ft IMC and 500 ft VMC stabilization criteria to prevent runway excursion and hard landings.
checklist: Verify aircraft is on published lateral localizer beam (deviation < 1 dot).
Verify vertical sink rate does not exceed 1,000 ft/min below 1,000 ft AGL.
Confirm landing gear down and locked, landing flaps fully deployed.
Confirm airspeed stabilized within -5 to +10 knots of calculated Vref.
Issue immediate go-around directive if parameters are not stabilized at or below decision gate.
rationale: Over 68% of commercial landing accidents stem from unstabilized approach profiles. Immediate go-around execution eliminates runway excursion risks.
incidentCase: Flight AIC2417 encountered windshear at 1,400 ft resulting in a 1,900 fpm descent rate; controller prompt detection allowed safe climb to 4,000 ft.

title: Airspace Sterile Buffer for Emergency Squawk 7700
summary: Immediate altitude sanitization, radio frequency protection, and priority emergency routing protocols.
checklist: Acknowledge 7700 transmission within 5 seconds on active frequency.
Establish 2,000 ft vertical and 5 NM lateral sterile cylinder around target.
Reroute conflicting traffic to auxiliary waypoints or entry holding.
Confirm crew intentions (immediate divert, fuel dump, or visual approach).
Stage Airport Rescue & Fire Fighting (ARFF) at designated rapid-exit taxiway.
rationale: ICAO Annex 11 mandates unconditional priority for aircraft declaring emergency distress to maximize survivability envelopes.
incidentCase: VTI812 experienced cabin pressure loss at FL280; rapid descent to 10,000 ft was accommodated with zero traffic conflicts due to early corridor clearing.

title: Convective Weather & Windshear Operations
summary: Handling severe monsoonal storm cells, microbursts, and rapid runway wind shifts at Hyderabad.
checklist: Monitor Doppler radar echo intensity and microburst alerts within 15 NM of VOHS.
Update active METAR and SPECI reports immediately upon wind shifts >= 10 knots.
Switch runway duty heading when tailwind component exceeds 5 knots.
Coordinate with adjacent sectors to enact minimum 20 NM spacing during holding.
Broadcast pilot-reported windshear (PIREP) to all aircraft on frequency without delay.
rationale: Sudden microburst downbursts can induce airframe sink rates exceeding 3,500 ft/min. Proactive runway switching prevents tailwind overrun incidents.
incidentCase: During pre-monsoon squall line over Shamshabad, three successive flights safely entered TEBUR holding while runway 27 was transitioned to runway 09.

title: Holding Stack Management & Separation Protocols
summary: Maintaining safe 1,000-foot vertical intervals in busy terminal holding stacks at TEBUR and OPROK.
checklist: Assign holding levels in standard 1,000 ft vertical increments (e.g. FL70, FL80, FL90).
Require verbal altitude vacancy report before descending next aircraft in stack.
Cross-check Mode C transponder telemetry before confirming step-down clearance.
Track estimated holding delay and issue revised Expect Approach Times (EAT) every 10 min.
Provide divert clearance immediately when flight indicates minimum divert fuel (BINGO fuel).
rationale: Vertical ladder management in holding stacks eliminates wake turbulence encounters and ensures rapid sequential feeds into the final approach course.
incidentCase: Six inbound flights stacked at TEBUR were sequentially stepped down and landed with average turnaround interval of only 2.5 minutes.

title: Loss of Surveillance Telemetry & Target Coasting
summary: Operating rules when ADS-B or Mode S packets drop out in terminal maneuvering airspace.
checklist: Verify if dropout is single-packet glitch or sustained (> 15 seconds) loss.
Enable SkyWatch dead-reckoning trajectory projection on controller display.
Instruct flight crew to recycle transponder code and check altitude reporting switch.
Corroborate with primary radar returns and voice position reports over mandatory fixes.
Increase procedural separation buffer to 10 NM until positive surveillance is restored.
rationale: Dead-reckoning projections maintain situational awareness while procedural separation buffers guarantee safety during radio frequency or equipment anomalies.
incidentCase: AXB539 experienced transponder power glitch north of Hyderabad; dead-reckoning projection kept spacing accurate until pilot recycled Mode S.
